label: thm
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm}
    For every $n\geq 1$, there exist knots $K$ and $K'$ such that
    \[
    \mathcal{J}(K)=\mathcal{J}(K') \qquad \mbox{and} \qquad
    \mathrm{LG}_{K}^{(n)}(q^\alpha,q)\neq \mathrm{LG}_{K'}^{(n)}(q^\alpha,q).
    \]
head: environment

label: cor
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor}
    For every integer $n\geq 1$, there does not exist a function $\Phi_n$ on the image of the colored Jones function such that for all knots $K$,
    \[
    \mathrm{LG}^{(n)}_K(q^\alpha,q)=\Phi_n(\mathcal{J}(K)).
    \]
head: environment

label: cor2
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor2}
    For every $n\geq 1$ and $N\geq2$, there exist knots $K_1,\dots, K_N$ with equal colored Jones sequences $\mathcal{J}(K_1)=\dots = \mathcal{J}(K_N)$ but their $n$-th colored Links--Gould polynomials $\mathrm{LG}_{K_1}^{(n)}, \dots, \mathrm{LG}_{K_N}^{(n)}$ are pairwise distinct.
head: environment

label: lem.CJ
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem.CJ}
    For any integer $j$, the following equalities hold
    \[
    \mathcal{J}(L)=\mathcal{J}(M) \qquad \mbox{and} \qquad
    \mathcal{J}(L^{(2,2j+1)})=\mathcal{J}(M^{(2,2j+1)}).
    \]
head: environment

title: Lemma
body_md:
There does not exist a function $\Phi$ on the set of $\mathbbm Z[q,q^{-1}]$-sequences such that
    \[
    \mathrm{LG}_K(q^\alpha,q)=\Phi(\mathcal{J}(K))
    \]
    for all $K$. In particular, $\mathrm{LG}$ is not determined by $\mathcal{J}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
It suffices to exhibit $L=C^{(2,1)}$ and $M=KT^{(2,1)}$ as a pair for which the colored Jones functions are equal, but which are distinguished by the Links--Gould polynomial. The first claim is exactly the statement of Lemma \ref{lem.CJ}. Now consider their difference of Links--Gould polynomials and apply \eqref{eq.LGcable},
    \[
    \mathrm{LG}_L(q^\alpha,q)-\mathrm{LG}_M(q^\alpha,q)=
    -A^{(2)}_{1,0}(q^\alpha,q)\left(\mathrm{LG}^{(2)}_C(q^{2\alpha},q)-\mathrm{LG}^{(2)}_{KT}(q^{2\alpha},q)\right).
    \]
    Since $\mathrm{LG}^{(2)}$ distinguishes $C$ from $KT$, and $A^{(2)}_{1,0}$ is nonzero, $\mathrm{LG}$ distinguishes $L$ and $M$.
head: environment

label: lem.fusion
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem.fusion}
    The nonzero values of $\widetilde{m}^{(n)}_{k,\ell}$ are given by Table \ref{table.fusion}. In particular, there are $3n$ isotypic components and $V(0,2\alpha+n-1)$ has multiplicity one.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We refer to the decomposition rule \cite[Lem.3.9]{GHKKW}. Although it is stated for $\alpha$, $\beta$, and $1$ being $\mathbbm Z$-linearly independent, it holds even when $\alpha=\beta$ under our standing assumption $\alpha\notin \frac{1}{2}\mathbbm Z$ so that all weights are typical. In our case, the isomorphism is 
    \begin{equation*}
        \begin{aligned}
        V(n-1,\alpha)^{\otimes 2}\cong&~ 
V(2n-1,2\alpha) \\
  &\oplus \bigoplus_{k=0}^{2n-2} V\left(k, 2\alpha+n-1+
\lfloor \tfrac{2-k}{2} \rfloor\right) \oplus
V\left(k, 2\alpha+n-1 + \lfloor \tfrac{1-k}{2} \rfloor\right).
    \end{aligned}
    \end{equation*}
    There is a unique maximum $k=2n-1$ summand $V(2n-1,2\alpha)$. For even indices $k=2r$, where the integer $r$ varies from $0$ to $n-1$, the summands are  
    \[
    V(2r, 2\alpha+n-r) \oplus
V(2r, 2\alpha+n-r-1).
    \]
     For odd indices $k=2r+1$ where $r$ varies from $0$ to $n-2$, the summands are 
    \[
    V(2r+1, 2\alpha+n-1-r) \oplus
V(2r+1, 2\alpha+n-1 -r).
    \]
    The table organizes these components.
head: environment

label: lem.FTisot
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We apply naturality of the RT construction on each inclusion and projection map, see for example \cite[Lem.2.2]{GHKKW}. Then for each $s$ and $t$, 
    \[
    F_T\circ i_s = i_s\circ F_{U,T}\qquad \mbox{and} \qquad p_t \circ F_T= F_{U,T}\circ p_t.
    \]
    Hence, we have the scalar action
    \[
    (F_T)_{s,t}=p_s\circ F_T\circ i_t=\delta_{s,t}\, \mathrm{LG}^{(k+1)}(q^{2\alpha+\ell},q).
    \]
    The second claim follows from expanding $P_{(k,\ell)}=\sum_{s} i_s\circ p_s$ and again applying naturality.
head: environment

label: lem.cisot
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
As before, set $U=V(k,2\alpha+\ell)$. For each $s$, we have
    \[
    \theta_{V\otimes V}i_s=i_s\theta_{U} \qquad \mbox{and} \qquad c^2=\theta_{V\otimes V}(\theta_V^{-1}\otimes \theta_V^{-1})\,\mathrm{id}_{V^{\otimes 2}} = \theta_V^{-2}\theta_{V\otimes V}\,\mathrm{id}_{V^{\otimes 2}}.
    \]
    Since $c$ is an intertwiner, we may write 
    \[
    (c_{k,\ell}^2)_{s,t}= p_s \circ c^2\circ i_t = \delta_{s,t}\,\frac{\theta_U}{\theta_V^2}=\delta_{s,t}\,\lambda_{k,\ell}.
    \]
    Taking $j$-th powers and multiplying by $c_{k\ell}$ yields the desired identity.
head: environment

label: prop.cable
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop.cable}
    Let $K$ be a zero-framed knot. Then for every $j\geq0$,
    \[
    \mathrm{LG}_{K^{(2,2j+1)}}(q^\alpha,q)=\theta_V^{-(2j+1)}\sum_{k,\ell\geq 0} \lambda_{k,\ell}^j\,\widetilde{A}_{k,\ell}^{(n)}(q^\alpha,q)\,  \mathrm{Tr}_{M^{(n)}_{k,\ell}}(c_{k,\ell})\, \mathrm{LG}_K^{(k+1)}(q^{2\alpha+\ell},q),
    \]
    where $\mathrm{Tr}_{M^{(n)}_{k,\ell}}$ is the trace of linear maps on $M^{(n)}_{k,\ell}$ as a vector space. Moreover, for $(k, \ell) = (0, n-1)$, the trace $\mathrm{Tr}_{M^{(n)}_{k,\ell}}(c_{k,\ell})$ is nonzero.
head: environment

label: eq.trtr
title: Proof
body_md:
Let $T$ be a $(1,1)$-tangle representative of $K$ and $F_T$ the RT operator for $T$ colored by $V^{\otimes 2}$. Equivalently, we may consider the $(2,0)$-cabling of $T$ and color it by $V$. The $(2,2j+1)$-cabling of $K$ is then presented by $F_T\circ c^{2j+1}$ and its modified trace satisfies
    \begin{align}\label{eq.trtr}
        \mathsf{tr}_{V\otimes V}(F_T\circ c^{2j+1}) = \mathsf{tr}_V(\mathrm{ptr}_V(F_T\circ c^{2j+1})).
    \end{align}
    We proceed by evaluating each side of the equality.

    For the left-hand side, we apply the channeling identity \eqref{eq.channel}, followed by Lemmas \ref{lem.FTisot} and \ref{lem.cisot}, and cyclicity of the modified trace
    \begin{equation*}
        \begin{aligned}
            \mathsf{tr}_{V\otimes V}(F_T\circ c^{2j+1}) &=\sum_{k,\ell\geq0}\mathsf{tr}_{V\otimes V}(F_T\circ c^{2j+1}\circ P_{(k,\ell)})
            \\
            &=
            \sum_{k,\ell\geq0} \mathrm{LG}_K^{(k+1)}(q^{2\alpha+\ell},q)\, \lambda_{k,\ell}^j \mathsf{tr}_{V\otimes V}(c\circ P_{(k,\ell)})
            \\
            &=
            \sum_{k,\ell\geq0} \mathrm{LG}_K^{(k+1)}(q^{2\alpha+\ell},q)\, \lambda_{k,\ell}^j \sum_s \mathsf{tr}_{U}(p_s \circ c \circ i_s)
            \\
            &=
            \sum_{k,\ell\geq0} \mathrm{LG}_K^{(k+1)}(q^{2\alpha+\ell},q)\, \lambda_{k,\ell}^j \sum_s c_{ss} \mathsf{tr}_{U}(\mathrm{id}_U)
            \\
            &=
            \sum_{k,\ell\geq0} \mathsf{d}(V(k,2\alpha+\ell))\, \mathrm{LG}_K^{(k+1)}(q^{2\alpha+\ell},q)\, \lambda_{k,\ell}^j \mathrm{Tr}_{M^{(n)}_{k,\ell}}(c_{k,\ell}).
        \end{aligned}
    \end{equation*}
    To resolve the right-hand side of \eqref{eq.trtr}, we adjust the $(1,1)$-tangle diagram associated to $\mathrm{ptr}_V(F_T\circ c^{2j+1})$ so that it has zero writhe by introducing a framing correction. We have
    \[
    \mathrm{ptr}_V(F_T\circ c^{2j+1}) = \theta_V^{2j+1}\mathrm{ptr}_V(\theta_V^{-(2j+1)}\, F_T\circ c^{2j+1})= \theta_V^{2j+1}\,\mathrm{LG}_{K^{(2,2j+1)}}^{(n)}(q^\alpha,q) \,\mathrm{id}_{V}
    \]
    which when composed with $\mathsf{tr}_V$ gives $\theta_V^{2j+1}\,\mathrm{LG}_{K^{(2,2j+1)}}^{(n)}(q^\alpha,q) \,\mathsf{d}(V)$.

    Combining both sides, and recalling $\widetilde{A}^{(n)}_{k,\ell}$ from \eqref{eq.A}, we now have the desired identity
    \begin{align*}
        \theta_V^{2j+1}\,\mathrm{LG}_{K^{(2,2j+1)}}^{(n)}(q^\alpha,q)\, \mathsf{d}(V) &= \sum_{k,\ell} \mathsf{d}(V(k,2\alpha+\ell))\, \mathrm{LG}_K^{(k+1)}(q^{2\alpha+\ell},q)\, \lambda_{k,\ell}^j \mathrm{Tr}_{M^{(n)}_{k,\ell}}(c_{k,\ell})
        \\
        \mathrm{LG}_{K^{(2,2j+1)}}^{(n)}(q^\alpha,q) &=\theta_V^{-(2j+1)} \sum_{k,\ell\geq0} \lambda_{k,\ell}^j \frac{\mathsf{d}(V(k,2\alpha+\ell))}{\mathsf{d}(V)} \mathrm{Tr}_{M^{(n)}_{k,\ell}}(c_{k,\ell}) \mathrm{LG}_K^{(k+1)}(q^{2\alpha+\ell},q).
    \end{align*}

    To prove the latter claim, we recall from Lemma \ref{lem.fusion} that $V(0,2\alpha+n-1)$ has multiplicity one. Since the braiding is invertible, each matrix $c_{k,\ell}$ must be invertible. In particular, $\mathrm{Tr}_{M^{(n)}_{0,n-1}}(c_{0,n-1})=c_{0,n-1}$ is invertible and hence nonzero.
head: environment

label: lem.lambda
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Evaluating $\lambda_{k,\ell}$, defined in Lemma \ref{lem.cisot}, with $\theta_V$ as in \eqref{eq.mdth} gives the prescribed value.
    We check the coefficient of $\alpha$ which is determined by $k+2\ell$. In Table \ref{table.fusion}, the value $k+2\ell$ in each row is $2n-2$, $2n$, $2n-1$, and again $2n-1$. Within each row, or the last pair of rows, we consider the constant term in the exponent of $q$, determined by $\ell(k+\ell+1)$. We verify that these are row-wise distinct for each pair $(k,\ell)$.
    \[
    \begin{array}{ccccc}
        k & \ell & \text{range} & k+2\ell& \ell(k+\ell+1)\\
        \hline
        2r   & n-1-r & 0\leq r\leq n-1 & 2n-2& n(n-1)-r(r+1)\\
        2r   & n-r   & 0\leq r\leq n-1 & 2n& n(n+1)-r(r+1) \\
        2r+1 & n-1-r & 0\leq r\leq n-2 & 2n-1& n^2-(r+1)^2 \\
        2n-1 & 0     & - &2n-1& 0
        \end{array}
    \]
    Note that $\ell(k+\ell+1)>0$ in the third row and is distinct from the value $0$ in the fourth row.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Suppose for the sake of a contradiction that 
    \[
    \mathrm{LG}^{(n)}_{L^{(2,2j+1)}}(q^\alpha,q)=\mathrm{LG}^{(n)}_{M^{(2,2j+1)}}(q^\alpha,q)
    \]
    for all integers $0\leq j \leq 3n-1$. For each $j$, applying Proposition \ref{prop.cable} and taking the difference of these polynomials implies
    \[
    0=\theta_V^{-(2j+1)}\sum_{k,\ell\geq0} \lambda_{k,\ell}^j\widetilde{A}_{k,\ell}^{(n)}\mathrm{Tr}_{M^{(n)}_{k,\ell}}(c_{k,\ell})\left(\mathrm{LG}_{L}^{(k+1)}(q^{2\alpha+\ell},q)-\mathrm{LG}_{M}^{(k+1)}(q^{2\alpha+\ell},q)\right).
    \]
    Normalize out the ribbon factor and set 
    \[D_{k,\ell}=\widetilde{A}_{k,\ell}^{(n)}\mathrm{Tr}_{M^{(n)}_{k,\ell}}(c_{k,\ell})\left(\mathrm{LG}_{L}^{(k+1)}(q^{2\alpha+\ell},q)-\mathrm{LG}_{M}^{(k+1)}(q^{2\alpha+\ell},q)\right)\]
    so that over all $j$ we have a $3n\times 3n$ system
    \[
    \sum_{k,\ell\geq 0 } D_{k,\ell}\lambda^j_{k,\ell}=0.
    \]
    Choose an ordering of the isotypic components $V(k,2\alpha+\ell)=V_i$ and assign the same ordering to $\lambda_{k,\ell}=\lambda_i$ and $D_{k,\ell}=D_i$. This realizes a Vandermonde system
    \[
\begin{pmatrix}
1 & 1 & \cdots & 1 \\
\lambda_1 & \lambda_2 & \cdots & \lambda_{3n} \\
\vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\
\lambda_1^{3n-1} & \lambda_2^{3n-1} & \cdots & \lambda_{3n}^{3n-1}
\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}
D_1 \\
D_2 \\
\vdots \\
D_{3n}
\end{pmatrix}=0.
\]
The determinant of the matrix of $(\lambda_i^j)_{ij}$ is $\prod_{i<j}(\lambda_j-\lambda_i)$, which is nonzero by Lemma \ref{lem.lambda}. Hence, $D_i=0$ for all $i$.

Now consider $(k,\ell)=(0,n-1)$. Recall that $\widetilde{A}^{(n)}_{k,\ell}$ is nonzero and from Proposition \ref{prop.cable} that $\mathrm{Tr}_{M^{(n)}_{k,\ell}}(c_{k,\ell})$ is nonzero as well. 
Finally, the Links--Gould polynomial in $(q^\alpha,q)$ distinguishes $L$ from $M$.
Hence, for $(k,\ell)=(0,n-1)$,
\[
D_{k,\ell}=\widetilde{A}_{k,\ell}^{(n)}\mathrm{Tr}_{M^{(n)}_{k,\ell}}(c_{k,\ell})\left(\mathrm{LG}_{L}^{(k+1)}(q^{2\alpha+\ell},q)-\mathrm{LG}_{M}^{(k+1)}(q^{2\alpha+\ell},q)\right)\neq 0
\]
and we have reached a contradiction. There must be some $0\leq j\leq 3n-1$ such that $\mathrm{LG}^{(n)}_{L^{(2,2j+1)}}(q^\alpha,q)\neq\mathrm{LG}^{(n)}_{M^{(2,2j+1)}}(q^\alpha,q)$. Moreover, $\mathcal{J}(L^{(2,2j+1)})=\mathcal{J}(M^{(2,2j+1)})$ by Lemma \ref{lem.CJ}.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $n\geq 1$. Let $A$ and $B$ be a pair of knots witnessing Theorem \ref{thm} so that $\mathcal{J}(A)=\mathcal{J}(B)$ and $\mathrm{LG}^{(n)}_A(q^\alpha,q)\neq\mathrm{LG}^{(n)}_{B}(q^\alpha,q)$. Let $K_m=A^{\# m-1}\#B^{\# N-m}$ for $1\leq m\leq N$. Multiplicativity of the Jones polynomial implies $\mathcal{J}(K_1)=\dots =\mathcal{J}(K_N)$.

    Similarly, multiplicativity of Links--Gould polynomials under connected sums gives
    \[
    LG^{(n)}_{K_m}(q^\alpha,q)=(\mathrm{LG}^{(n)}_{A}(q^\alpha,q))^{m-1}\cdot (\mathrm{LG}^{(n)}_{B}(q^\alpha,q))^{N-m}
    \] 
    Now \cite[Thm.1.3]{GHKKW} states $\mathrm{LG}^{(n)}_K(1,q)=1$ for every knot $K$. In particular, $\mathrm{LG}^{(n)}_A(q^\alpha,q)$ and $\mathrm{LG}^{(n)}_B(q^\alpha,q)$ are nonzero. 
    
    Suppose for contradiction that $LG^{(n)}_{K_s}=LG^{(n)}_{K_t}$ for some $s\neq t$. Let $x=\mathrm{LG}^{(n)}_{A}\cdot (\mathrm{LG}^{(n)}_{B})^{-1}$. By our assumption 
    \[
    \frac{(\mathrm{LG}^{(n)}_{A}(q^\alpha,q))^{s-1}\cdot (\mathrm{LG}^{(n)}_{B}(q^\alpha,q))^{N-s}}{(\mathrm{LG}^{(n)}_{A}(q^\alpha,q))^{t-1}\cdot (\mathrm{LG}^{(n)}_{B}(q^\alpha,q))^{N-t}} = x^{s-t}=1.
    \]
    This implies $x$ is a root of unity in $\mathbbm Q(q^\alpha,q)$ and hence $x=\pm 1$. If $x=1$, then this contradicts $\mathrm{LG}^{(n)}_A(q^\alpha,q)\neq\mathrm{LG}^{(n)}_B(q^\alpha,q)$. If $x=-1$, then this violates the specialization property $\mathrm{LG}^{(n)}_K(1,q)=1$. Therefore the colored Links--Gould polynomials of $K_1,\dots, K_N$ are pairwise distinct.
head: environment
